content:
Penguins cannot fly through the air like most birds. They are flightless birds that have evolved to be excellent swimmers instead.

However, penguins are sometimes described as "flying" underwater because they use their wings (flippers) to propel themselves through water in a motion very similar to how other birds fly through air. They're incredibly graceful and fast swimmers - some species can reach speeds of up to 22 mph (35 km/h) underwater.

So while penguins can't soar through the sky, they've mastered a different kind of "flight" beneath the waves!
